eyebrow: Azure & AWS Cloud Security Engineering · Chapter 4
titlePlain: NSGs and Security Groups: the Same Idea,
subtitle: Lesson 13 · Network Security Across Both Clouds

code:
az network nsg rule create \
  --resource-group rg-prod \
  --nsg-name nsg-web-subnet \
  --name Allow-HTTPS-Inbound \
  --priority 100 \
  --direction Inbound \
  --access Allow \
  --protocol Tcp \
  --source-address-prefixes Internet \
  --destination-port-ranges 443
caption: Priority 100 is evaluated before the built-in DenyAllInBound default at 65500.

code:
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress \
  --group-id sg-0abc123def456 \
  --protocol tcp \
  --port 443 \
  --cidr 0.0.0.0/0

# source can also be another SG:
# --source-group sg-0db-tier
caption: No priority field — SGs are allow-only, so every attached group's rules are unioned.

eyebrow: AWS NACL rule — the real NSG analog
code:
aws ec2 create-network-acl-entry \
  --network-acl-id acl-0123abcd \
  --ingress \
  --rule-number 100 \
  --protocol tcp \
  --port-range From=443,To=443 \
  --cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 \
  --rule-action allow
caption: Stateless — the outbound return traffic needs its own explicit rule.
